title: Linear-Time Decidability of Palindromes
statement: The language of binary words equal to their reversals is decidable in time $c(n+1)$ for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$: there is a finite deterministic multi-tape Turing machine that, on every binary input of length $n$, halts within that many steps and outputs $1$ exactly for palindromes and $0$ otherwise.
replaced:
The language of binary palindromes — the set of words $x \in \{0,1\}^*$ with
$x^{R} = x$ — lies in $\mathrm{DTIME}(n+1)$: there exist a constant $c$ and a
multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet that, on every input of length
$n$, halts within $c\,(n+1)$ steps and outputs true exactly when the input is a
palindrome, and false otherwise.
